'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Israel–Hamas war]]
**[[Siege of Khan Yunis]]
***[[Special forces of Israel|Israeli special forces]] raid [[Nasser Hospital]] in [[Khan Yunis]], the largest hospital still functioning in the [[Gaza Strip]]. At least one person is killed and eight others are reportedly injured during the raid. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2024/feb/15/israeli-troops-raid-nasser-hospital-southern-gaza (''The Guardian'')]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[2021–present United Kingdom cost-of-living crisis]]
**The [[United Kingdom]] enters a technical [[recession]], as a report issued by the [[Office for National Statistics]] stated that the economy shrunk in two consecutive quarters amid a slowdown in [[consumer spending]]. [https://www.cnbc.com/2024/02/15/uk-economy-slipped-into-technical-recession-at-the-end-of-2023.html (CNBC)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*Eleven people are killed and four more injured during a fire at a [[paint]] factory in [[New Delhi]], [[India]]. [https://apnews.com/article/fire-paint-factory-new-delhi-india-alipur-dead-185fa14e9c19800752524dbf3be49d04 (AP)]
*Nine [[firefighters]] are injured when a [[truck]] [[fuel tank]] explodes in the [[Wilmington, Los Angeles|Wilmington]] neighborhood of [[Los Angeles]], [[California]], [[United States]]. [https://amp.theguardian.com/us-news/2024/feb/15/los-angeles-firefighters-truck-fuel-explosion (''The Guardian'')]

'''International relations'''
*[[Russia–United States relations]], [[Russia and weapons of mass destruction]]
**The [[Kremlin]] dismisses a warning by the [[United States]] that [[Russia]] intends to imminently place [[nuclear weapon]]s in space as a "malicious fabrication". The claims were widely circulated yesterday by [[ABC News (United States)|ABC News]] and the ''[[New York Times]]'' after [[Speaker of the United States House of Representatives|U.S. House Speaker]] [[Mike Johnson (Louisiana politician)|Mike Johnson]] warned of a "serious national security threat". [https://www.reuters.com/world/kremlin-dismisses-us-warning-about-russian-nuclear-capability-space-2024-02-15/ (Reuters)] [https://www.reuters.com/world/us/us-congressional-intelligence-chair-warns-serious-national-security-threat-2024-02-14/ (Reuters 2)]
**[[Reuters]] reports that it is highly unlikely that [[Russia]] intends to put a [[nuclear warhead]] in space. The [[antisatellite weapon]] is more likely a [[Nuclear power in space|nuclear-powered space-based device]] that utilizes [[electronic warfare]] to blind, jam or fry the electronics inside targets. [https://www.reuters.com/technology/space/russia-seen-highly-unlikely-put-nuclear-warhead-space-2024-02-15/ (Reuters)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Same-sex marriage in Greece]]
**The [[Hellenic Parliament]] votes 176–76 to legalise [[same-sex marriage]] and [[same-sex adoption|adoption]], making it the first [[Eastern Orthodoxy|Eastern Orthodox]] country to do so. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2024/feb/15/greece-becomes-first-orthodox-christian-country-to-legalise-same-sex-marriage (''The Guardian'')]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2024 Wellingborough by-election]], [[2024 Kingswood by-election]]
** In the United Kingdom, the [[Labour Party (UK)|Labour Party]]'s [[Gen Kitchen]] and [[Damien Egan]] respectively flip the seats of [[Wellingborough (UK Parliament constituency)|Wellingborough]] and [[Kingswood (UK Parliament constituency)|Kingswood]] from the [[Conservative Party (UK)|Conservative Party]] in two [[by-elections]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/live/uk-politics-68277176 (BBC News)]

'''Science and technology'''
*''[[Odysseus (lunar lander)|Odysseus]]'', the first [[United States|US]] [[lunar lander]] since the unsuccessful [[Peregrine Mission One]], is launched at the [[Kennedy Space Center]] [[Florida]], [[United States]]. [https://www.space.com/spacex-launch-im-1-private-moon-landing-mission (Space.com)]

'''Sports'''
*In US women's college basketball, [[2023–24 Iowa Hawkeyes women's basketball team|Iowa's]] [[Caitlin Clark]] becomes the [[List of NCAA Division I women's basketball career scoring leaders|career scoring leader]] in [[NCAA Division I]], surpassing the record previously held by current [[Women's National Basketball Association|WNBA]] and former [[Washington Huskies women's basketball|Washington]] star [[Kelsey Plum]] during Iowa's 106–89 win over [[2023–24 Michigan Wolverines women's basketball team|Michigan]].
